subject: c12-math
note: Official CBSE Mathematics theory paper: 80 marks. The 2026-27 syllabus explicitly states that there is no chapter-wise weightage; all chapters should be covered. Internal assessment is separate: 20 marks.
mistakes: Relations and Functions: confusing relation properties or treating one-to-one and onto as the same condition.
Inverse Trigonometric Functions: ignoring the principal-value branch and writing identities outside their valid ranges.
Matrices and Determinants: changing multiplication order or applying determinant/adjoint rules as if matrices were scalars.
Continuity and Differentiability: skipping domain restrictions and chain-rule factors.
Applications of Derivatives: solving critical-point problems without checking endpoints or the required first/second derivative conditions.
Integrals: choosing a method mechanically; identify substitution, partial fractions, by-parts or standard form before calculating.
Definite integrals: losing limits or using symmetry properties without checking the interval and function.
Differential Equations: losing the constant of integration or applying the integrating factor incorrectly.
Vectors and 3D: confusing dot and cross products or mixing vector and Cartesian line forms.
Linear Programming: drawing an incorrect feasible region or checking only one vertex.
Probability: confusing conditional probability with ordinary probability and using independence without justification.
order: Complete Relations and Functions, Inverse Trigonometric Functions, Matrices and Determinants first to establish the algebraic base.
Move through Calculus in sequence: Continuity and Differentiability → Applications of Derivatives → Integrals → Applications of Integrals → Differential Equations.
Study Vectors and Three-dimensional Geometry together.
Finish Linear Programming and Probability after the main calculus/algebra sequence.
Maintain a separate error log for algebraic slips, domain/range errors, sign errors and method-selection errors.
Practise mixed questions regularly because the official syllabus has no chapter-wise weightage.
Use timed full-paper practice and review every unsolved or partially solved question, not only final-answer mistakes.
